title: Electricity & Heat
page_title: Electricity & Heat | Edexcel IGCSE Science (Double Award) Revision Notes 2017

blocks.md:
- A **current** passing through a resistor (or wire) results in the **electrical transfer of energy**

  - As explained in [Charge & current,](https://www.savemyexams.com/igcse/science/edexcel/double-award/17/physics/revision-notes/electricity/current-potential-difference-and-resistance/charge-and-current/) current is the **rate of flow of charge**
- The temperature of a resistor increases due to the **collisions** of the **free electrons** within the wire
- Some of the **energy is dissipated** into the surroundings by **heating**

- This heating effect is **utilised** in many domestic contexts, including:

  - Electric **heaters**
  - Electric **ovens**
  - Electric **hob**
  - **Toasters**
  - **Kettles**

blocks.text: Heating a pan on an electrical hob

blocks.md: ***The heating effect of current can be used for many applications such as electric hobs***
